population.label: Middle-Eastern / Jordanian

scale.source: Cephalometric Analysis, p. 614: magnification adjusted with a radiopaque calibration ruler

curation.notes: Compared 2026-10-13 (norms:compare a vs b exit 1; self-test passed). All 4 means, SDs and n agreed; re-read at merge on the page image of Table 3 (PDF p. 3 = p. 615) and Table 2 for n 94: all agree. The only difference: ageBand (a none, b [18, 40]); settled [18, 40] (ruling, P18: adults over 18, p. 616, no upper age). Gonial and sum close (Ar-Go-Gn against the catalogue's Ar-Go-Me), saddle and articular same, as both readers. Set-level: selection mixed-occlusion (ruling, P37: 288 orthodontic patients before treatment, p. 614, split by ANB; both readers had class-I; superseded the same day by owner ruling KIMRANK-1: class-I, ranked as an ordinary Class I sample); population label the populations list's own (b had written its own label; moved the same day to the new population 'jordanian', owner ruling JORDAN-1); ageMin 18 (b); scale true-size (both: calibration ruler, p. 614). Table 4's by-sex rows pool all three classes: caveat only (P19). jarabak-via-almaaitah2022 was not created: the paper quotes only two cut-offs for Jarabak's sum of angles, no mean or SD (both readers).

caveats: Norm group: the skeletal Class I group (ANB 2-4 degrees, p. 615) of 288 pretreatment orthodontic patients at Jordan University of Science and Technology clinics (p. 614). Class II (n 99) and Class III (n 95) groups in Table 3 are malocclusion groups and are not entered.

Ranked as an ordinary Class I sample (owner ruling KIMRANK-1, 13 Oct; replaces the P37 treatment-sample ruling of the same day): orthodontic patients before treatment, p. 614, picked for a skeletal Class I pattern; dental occlusion of the Class I group is not described.
ANB was used to pick the Class I group (2-4 degrees; Table 2, p. 615: Class I ANB 2.95 +/- 0.82, n 94) and is not entered as a norm (P45).

The whole sample was also restricted to an average maxillary-mandibular plane angle (MMPA 27 +/- 5 degrees, p. 614). The sum of polygon angles tracks vertical pattern, so its spread here is probably narrower than in an unselected sample; the paper itself links the similar sums across classes to this restriction (p. 617).

Sex: Table 4 (p. 616) gives men and women separately, but each pools Classes I, II and III together (men 142, women 146), so those rows are not a Class I norm and are not entered. Within Class I only both-sexes values are printed (Table 3).

Ages: adults only (over 18, p. 616). Mean age is given for the whole sample by sex only (women 21.24 +/- 2.72, men 22.94 +/- 3.28 years, p. 613-614), not for the Class I group; no upper age stated. Entries carry ageBand [18, 40] per the adult rule.
Gonion: Table 1 (p. 614) names point Gonion without saying whether it is anatomical or constructed; Figure 1 draws it at the mandibular angle where the ramus and Go-Gn lines meet.
Not in the catalogue: S-N, S-Ar, Ar-Go and Go-Gn lengths in mm (Table 3, p. 615). The catalogue's ratios #43 (S-N/Go-Me) and #44 (Ar-S/Ar-Go) are not printed and were not computed.
Upper and lower gonial angles (#37, #38), S-Go, N-Me and the Jarabak ratio (#40-#42) are not measured in this paper.
Film: lateral cephalograms hand traced (Orthoslice 1000 C with cephalostat, p. 614); head orientation (FH or natural head position) not stated; taken in centric occlusion.

Population: the paper calls its subjects Caucasians of the Jordanian population (p. 614); they are Jordanian adults, filed under their own population 'jordanian' (Middle-Eastern / Jordanian), owner ruling JORDAN-1, 13 Oct. They were first filed under 'caucasian', whose label speaks of European background.
Reference only, not entered: Class II and Class III columns of Table 3 (p. 615) and Table 4's by-sex rows (p. 616), which pool all three classes.
